messages:
alex_m: Pushed a short perf writeup from today's spike. p99 for a couple pods climbed to ~1.8s after the 09:00 deploy. Dump attached in thread.
julie: saw that too. initial hypothesis was kernel switch thrash + big prompts. any profiling traces?
matt_dev: I grabbed a sample trace from a pod: 
```
# tail_latency sample
request_id=rid-3347 context_len=12k microbatch=8 kernel=ampere-opt seq=4096 kv_hit=false
stage=compile kernel_switch=true tool_calls=0 generation_time=1.2s
postproc=0.45s
```

sre_ana: interesting kv_hit=false on many of these. are long prompts evicting the KV cache?
eva_research: we saw a bump in max_seq distribution after the new prompt templates rolled out; 99th perc went from 1.5k -> 6.8k, so kernel selection is flipping to the slower path mid-request sometimes.
alex_m: yep. correlates with kernel_switch=true. scheduler was picking small-batch kernels for earlier microbatches then switching to long-seq kernels when context grew — that switch is expensive.
julie: do we have batcher logs to show microbatch composition over time? I want to see if long-context requests are getting co-batched with short ones.
matt_dev: pulled microbatch traces: most p99s come from batches with 1 long prompt + N short ones. Batcher tries to pack to max_tokens and ends up increasing compilation overhead. snippet: 
```
batch_id=bb-776 members=[short, short, long] max_seq=8192 compile_cost=320ms
```

sre_ana: so two issues: kernel recompile / selection cost and KV cache misses. Also saw a few tool-calling loops (user prompt triggers tool -> tool returns prompt extension -> another tool call) but that's only ~8% of spikes.
eva_research: for kernel overhead we can add a heuristic: detect long-sequence first token and pre-select/prepare long-seq kernels so later microbatches don't trigger compile. basically pre-warm.
julie: agree. Also suggest a microbatch slicing rule: don't co-batch long (>4k) with short (<512). Either isolate or cap co-batch size when mix detected. quick patch idea: 
```
if any(seq_len>4096 for req in batch): enforce max_batch_size=4
```

matt_dev: quick mitigation: mark requests with seq_len>6k as "solo-path" and route them to dedicated slot with preloaded kernels and warm KV. cheaper than recompiling per pod.
alex_m: for KV, evictions are caused by per-request keyspace ballooning. short-term we can increase kv_capacity for pods serving experimental route. long-term we need shared LRU across worker shards or sticky routing by conversation id.
sre_ana: also found ~3 requests with >20 tool_calls in a loop before they hit our tool-call depth breaker. those amplified latency massively due to repeated generation and network calls. we should tighten loop detection and add early abort + fallback.
eva_research: added a regression check to eval harness: synthetic long-prompts + tool-call stress test. will flag model/kernel combos that recompile more than X times per 1000 requests.
julie: action items: 1) matt -> roll solo-path routing patch to canary today, 2) alex -> kv_capacity bump + metrics for kv_hit ratio, 3) eva -> add regression test in eval harness, 4) sre_ana -> tune tool-call depth breaker and alert on high loop rate.
matt_dev: canary ready, pushing in 15m. will monitor p95/p99 and compile_count metric.
infra-bot: deploy canary started: rollout/solo-path-v1 -> 10% traffic (pods=6). CI: green.
alex_m: thanks. will follow up with a short postmortem if canary reduces tail. otherwise we iterate on prewarm + batcher heuristics. :thumbsup:
